sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **26 of the official questions in Words in Context are this one** — 0 Easy, 0 Medium, 26 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- It is a Hard-level blank, and the choices are unusual or academic words, sometimes with an article attached ('a/an ___').
- Several choices share a general tone, positive or negative, so the tone of the sentence alone won't settle it.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Work out a precise meaning for the blank from the logic of the sentence, not just its tone.
- 2) Cross out the choices you know don't fit.
- 3) Between the ones left, choose the word whose exact meaning fits, even if it's the one you know less well.
- Don't eliminate an unfamiliar word just because it's unfamiliar.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick the word you recognize because it roughly fits, when the answer is an unfamiliar word that fits exactly.
Or you get caught by a word that looks or sounds like the idea you want but means something unrelated.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
